page_title: device configuration by scanning a QR code
page_content:
[TOC]

### I. Feature Overview

**Configure your device simply by scanning a QR code — no network connection required.**

Enter parameters on your phone to generate a QR code, then have the device camera scan it to apply the configuration. No SD card swapping, and no need to wait for the device to get online.

| Comparison | SD Card Import | Online Platform Provisioning | **QR Code Import** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Device needs network | No | **Yes (must be connected)** | **No** |
| Remove / insert SD card | Yes | No | No |
| Time per device | 1–2 minutes | Depends on platform response | **A few seconds** |

**Typical use case:** on a production line or in a warehouse, devices may not have a SIM card or network access yet. Scan in the device ID and platform address first — once powered on, the device can go online immediately.

### II. Prerequisites

- Device firmware supports QR code import (`M93Hv-APP-TQRC004.crc` or later).
- A 4G SIM card is inserted and the antenna is connected, and the device can establish a data connection (required to verify the platform connection after import).
- Sufficient ambient lighting; avoid strong reflections.

**About `qrcfg.txt`:** place this file — containing the single line `qrcfg_chn=1` — in the **root directory of the device's first disk partition** and the device will **keep scanning for QR codes continuously**. Download it here: [qrcfg.txt](http://pug2.4000329988.com/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&amp;sign=83164cf334653263529513e397bb03b5)

Even without this file, scanning still works — but the device will only accept a scan **within about 5 minutes of powering on**; after that, scanning no longer works.

> The value `1` in `qrcfg_chn=1` means camera channel 1 handles the scanning. M93Hv is a single-camera device, so keep this value at `1`.

### III. Tool Link and QR Code

**Tool link:** [Quick Configuration via QR Code](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/web/tools/qrconfig-en.html)

**QR code:**

**Printable version for stickers** (for the device body, manual, or packaging box; 1368×1488): [tool-qr-print.png](http://pug2.4000329988.com/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=a01a74ec0cbf8d9fe0dc83ad9bc1cb91 "[tool-qr-print.png")

### IV. Operating Steps

#### 1. Open the Configuration Tool

- **Mobile:** open the link directly in WeChat or a web browser.
- **PC:** open it with Chrome or Edge.

> **Tip:** once the page is open you can save it locally (Ctrl+S / File → Save Page As) and use the tool offline later.

![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=49866a3d54c392b32c4db048485e45db)

#### 2. Enter Parameters

There are four tabs at the top. **Fill in only what you need to change — fields left blank are not written to the device.**

| Tab | What to Enter |
| --- | --- |
| **Time Zone** | Your local time zone (UTC+8 for China) |
| **4G/5G** | APN, dial-up number, username and password (usually keep the defaults) |
| **Center Platform** | **Device ID**, platform address (IP or domain name) and port |
| **808 Platform** | Enable status, terminal ID, platform address, port and phone number |

> Use **English letters and digits only** for account names, passwords, APN and domain names — no Chinese characters or spaces.

![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=a72fd11078da118d6d686cb0e680ad5c)

#### 3. Click [Generate] to Create the QR Code

Click **[Generate]** at the bottom of the page. The QR code appears on screen together with the generated configuration below it, so you can check that everything is correct.

![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=9207c43291ac5d9c4cb43bbac1e90dfd)

#### 4. Scan the QR Code with the Device

- Place the QR code in the **center of the device's field of view** (the device only reads the central 80% of the frame; a code near the edge will not be read).
- Set screen brightness to **maximum**, keep a distance of about **20–40 cm**, and avoid glare or reflections on the screen.
- **Orientation does not matter** — horizontal, vertical or even upside down all work (this is a built-in feature of QR code technology).

Once scanned, the device emits a **beep** (similar to a WeChat scan), followed by a voice prompt reporting **import success and the device ID** — the configuration has been applied.

#### 5. Verify That It Took Effect

**If you configured 808 platform parameters, the device must be restarted** after a successful import. After restarting, check the platform to confirm the device shows as **online**.

> **Prerequisite:** the device must have a 4G SIM card inserted, the antenna connected, and a working 4G data connection. Otherwise it will not come online and the import cannot be verified.

### V. FAQ

| Issue | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Device fails to scan the QR code | ① Make sure the code is centered in the frame; ② check the distance (move to 20–40 cm); ③ the screen or environment may be too dark; ④ check for screen glare. Also confirm `qrcfg.txt` is in place, or that the device was powered on recently. |
| Cannot scan from a phone screenshot | Capture **only the QR code itself, including the surrounding white border** — do not capture the whole screen, which makes the code appear too small in the frame. |
| Device does not come online after import | ① For 808 platform configurations you **must restart** the device; ② confirm the device has a working 4G data connection; ③ make sure you scanned the latest code (after a successful import the device waits at least 3 seconds before scanning again). |
| Can it work without a SIM card or network? | **Yes.** That is the main value of this feature. But **verifying success** requires the device to have an active data connection. |
| Does enabling QR scanning affect other functions? | Yes. **When QR scanning is enabled, other AI functions (such as Motovis or Meitong) will not be activated.** |

### VI. Important Notes

1. For 808 platform configurations, the device **must be restarted** after import before it comes online.
2. Keep the QR code **centered and as large as possible**, with screen brightness at maximum, and avoid screen glare.
3. Scanning works in **night-vision (IR) mode**, but do not let the IR light shine directly onto the code — it may overexpose and obscure it.
4. **Enabling QR scanning prevents other AI functions from being activated.**
5. Repeated scanning of the same QR code is restricted (minimum 3-second interval).

> **Related documentation:** for importing a configuration from an SD card, or pushing one from the platform, see [Other Configuration Methods](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/web/#/13/64).
